title: Affine-base restriction maps for projective spectra of a graded algebra sheaf
statement: Let $X$ be a scheme and $\mathcal A=\bigoplus_{n\geq0}\mathcal A_n$ a graded $\mathcal O_X$-algebra whose homogeneous components are quasi-coherent, as in [def-nagata-relative-proj]. For every affine open $U\subseteq X$ put $P_U=\operatorname{Proj}(\Gamma(U,\mathcal A))$ [def-nagata-affine-proj], with $p_U:P_U\to U$ induced by $\mathcal O_X(U)\to\Gamma(U,\mathcal A)_0$. For affine opens $V\subseteq U$, the graded restriction homomorphism induces a canonical morphism $r^U_V:P_V\to P_U$ over $U$. This morphism identifies $P_V$ with the open subscheme $p_U^{-1}(V)$ over $V$. It is the identity when $V=U$ and satisfies $r^U_W=r^U_V\circ r^V_W$ whenever $W\subseteq V\subseteq U$ are affine opens.

proof.text: The homogeneous section subgroups of the input are ranges of linear maps, hence submodules. Their underlying additive groups carry the given internal grading. Use the identity graded homomorphisms to identify the Proj of this submodule grading with the specified local Proj, compatibly with its degree-zero base map.

Quasi-coherent affine section base change gives bijective total scalar extension. Decomposition and tensor/direct-sum commutation imply bijectivity in each degree. This proves gradeRestriction_baseChange and packages the actual section rings as source GradedAlgebraData. Apply its isPullback_relProjFunctor_map (which uses the affine Proj scalar-extension primitive and the affine spectrum inclusion identity). Transport along the identity grading isomorphisms using gradeIso_naturality and gradeIso_hom_base.
The restriction homomorphisms satisfy identity and composition by the sheaf functor laws. Proj.map_id and Proj.map_comp give the corresponding identity and composition for localTransition.
